newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission plans food safety unit.
newsitem.headline: Commission plans food safety unit.

text.p: The European Commission is planning to separate responsibilities for food safety and agricultural policy following an internal review prompted by the row over the handling of the mad cow crisis.

A Commission spokesman said Commission President Jacques Santer would announce the plans in a speech to the European Parliament's committee of inquiry into the disease, Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) late on Wednesday in Strasbourg.
The parliament is currently meeting in the easdtern French city.

The parliamentary committee's draft report accuses the Commission of trying to play down the dangers of BSE which caused consumer panic and a crisis in the beef industry when Britain announced last year that it could be transmitted to humans in the form of Creutzfeld Jakob Disease.
But the spokesman said the proposal to give separate commissioners responsibility for agriculture and food was not a response to the report but the result of the Commission's own review.
"The Commission has conducted its own internal review of BSE and the proposals arise from the results of that review and are not a reaction to the committee of inquiry," he said.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has backed the idea of a separate European Union food agency but Santer's proposal is for a 30-strong inspection team responsible for food safety and for ensuring that EU member states enforce EU laws, EU sources said.
